title: Order transfer through six for Williamson low-storage Runge–Kutta methods
shortTitle: Classical accuracy survives the exponential lift
oneLine: A division-free tensor identity transfers classical order through six; three explicit extra tests give a conditional criterion at order seven.
abstract: This anonymous mathematical candidate proves that every finite real Williamson low-storage Runge–Kutta coefficient list of classical order at most six retains at least that order under the specified left-multiplication exponential lift. An all-degree repeated-tail identity, polarisation and finite shuffle systems reduce ordered-flow coefficients to classical moments. The result covers zero and negative coefficients and repeated stage nodes. A conditional order-seven criterion reduces the next-order question to three extra tensor identities; automatic seventh-order transfer remains open. Written proofs are accompanied by exact internal replay, separate checker implementations and corruption controls. No external specialist review, independent external reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

narration: Classical accuracy survives the exponential lift. An Evidence Press briefing. Many equations describe rotations or other constrained matrices. Ordinary numerical updates can leave that constraint, while exponential updates preserve it. But matrix multiplication does not commute, so preserving the shape does not automatically preserve accuracy. This paper proves that a structured family is different. Take a Williamson low-storage Runge–Kutta method, with any finite number of stages. If its classical order is at most six, the specified exponential version has at least the same order. The argument allows zero and negative coefficients and repeated stage times. The proof starts with an identity for the ordered products produced by the updates. Small exact linear systems then show that the extra conditions follow from the familiar classical conditions. A continuous integration comparison identifies their exact target values. The package contains the written argument and exact checks of 197 ordered-tree coefficients. Separate internal implementations check prefixes and ranks, while deliberate corruption tests confirm that invalid certificates are rejected. A further result gives three explicit extra tests sufficient for order seven. It does not show that those tests follow automatically, and it does not settle the all-orders question. Nor does the paper promise better error constants or computational performance for a particular method. This is an anonymous, unrefereed mathematical candidate, not externally reproduced or formally verified. Published on 20 October 2026, its paper and evidence are linked on the Williamson order-transfer release at Evidence Press. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.
